rows.note: Use this for a shop or business bringing goods in and keeping them as sale stock, including stocking a warehouse with goods.

example.english: We stock new clothes every week.
example.traditional: 我哋間舖每個星期都入貨。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gaan1 pou3 mui5 go3 sing1 kei4 dou1 jap6 fo3

rows.note: Use 股票 for company shares or an investment in a company.

example.english: I bought stock in that company.
example.traditional: 我買咗嗰間公司嘅股票。
example.jyutping: ngo5 maai5 zo2 go2 gaan1 gung1 si1 ge3 gu2 piu3

rows.note: Use this when “stock” means to supply or provide someone or somewhere with the required goods or materials.

example.english: We stock schools across Hong Kong with stationery.
example.traditional: 我哋供應文具畀全港學校。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gung1 jing3 man4 geoi6 bei2 cyun4 gong2 hok6 haau6

rows.note: Use this specifically when “stock” means to store goods or materials for later use rather than supply them.

example.english: The warehouse will stock enough medical supplies for emergencies.
example.traditional: 倉庫會儲存足夠嘅醫療物資，以備不時之需。
example.jyutping: cong1 fu3 wui5 cyu4 cyun4 zuk1 gau3 ge3 ji1 liu4 mat6 zi1 ji5 bei6 bat1 si4 zi1 seoi1

rows.note: Use 存貨 as the all-purpose noun for goods kept ready for sale.

example.english: This stock hasn’t all been sold yet.
example.jyutping: ni1 pai1 cyun4 fo3 zung6 mei6 cing1 dak1 saai3

rows.note: Use 儲備 as the all-purpose noun for a supply kept for later use.

example.english: The company is keeping some masks in stock for emergencies.
example.traditional: 公司要留返啲口罩做儲備。
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 jiu3 lau4 faan1 di1 hau2 zaau3 zou6 cyu5 bei6

rows.note: Use 湯底 when stock means the base liquid for a soup or stew.

example.english: This restaurant’s beef-bone stock is really fragrant.
example.traditional: 呢間店嘅牛骨湯底好香。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 dim3 ge3 ngau4 gwat1 tong1 dai2 hou2 hoeng1
